Definition: from a compound of G2596 and a derivative of G3717 (compare G1357); something made fully upright, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (specially, good public administration):--very worthy deed.
BiblicalUsage: Katorthoma means a very worthy deed, a public good done well. Acts 24:2 has Tertullus flattering Felix, saying that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe flattery calls any deed worthy, but God weighs what was actually done.
